item.title: Don’t Mess with the Houthis
item.description: On the morning of 20 September 2026 — Chicago time — I was on “Switzerland” talking with Tom Switzer about what appeared to be an imminent US attack against the Houthis.
item.dc:creator: John J. Mearsheimer
item.content:encoded:
On the morning of 20 September 2026 — Chicago time — I was on “Switzerland” talking with Tom Switzer about what appeared to be an imminent US attack against the Houthis. President Trump was under tremendous pressure from Saudi Arabia to come to its aid in its war with the Houthis.

I laid out in considerable detail why the US has no viable military option against the Houthis, and thus launching military strikes against them would be a fool’s errand. Thankfully, President Trump’s advisers understood that we could not defeat the Houthis and they convinced him to call off the attack, which he did late that same day.

Of course, the Saudis, who are being battered by the Houthis, are beyond angry with President Trump, who cannot figure out how to end either the disastrous war against Iran he started on 28 February 2026 or the new war that broke out between the Houthis and the Saudis on 13 July 2026 and then seriously escalated on 8 September 2026.

item.title: What Is An”Ugly Victory”?
item.description: On 17 September 2026, I was on Glenn Diesen’s popular podcast talking about the war in Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: John J. Mearsheimer
item.content:encoded: On 17 September 2026, I was on Glenn Diesen’s popular podcast talking about the war in Ukraine. We focused much attention on how the war is likely to end and what I mean when I say that Russia is likely to win an “ugly victory.” We also discussed how Russia is now waging both its ground war on the front lines and its strategic bombing campaign against Ukraine and how those two dimension of the Russian offensive relate to each other. We also spoke about the important article that Iuliia Mendel, President Zelensky’s first press secretary published recently in The Spectator. It maintains that Ukraine is pursuing national suicide by continuing its war against Russia, and backs up that argument with facts that can only be described as shocking. In essence it portrays a truly grim picture of the state of affairs in Ukraine.

item.title: Trump’s Not So Creative Destruction
item.description: On 15 September 2026, I was on “Judging Freedom.” The Judge and I talked about the Iran war, which is going from bad to worse for the US now that the Houthis have closed the Bab al-Mandab Strait and are destroying critical Saudi oil facilities.
item.dc:creator: John J. Mearsheimer
item.content:encoded:
On 15 September 2026, I was on “Judging Freedom.” The Judge and I talked about the Iran war, which is going from bad to worse for the US now that the Houthis have closed the Bab al-Mandab Strait and are destroying critical Saudi oil facilities. The flow of Saudi oil into global markets has been greatly reduced as a result, which obviously harms the international economy.

Also, the Judge and I were recently in Russia together where we met and spoke with numerous Russians, including Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov. We reflected on what we learned on that trip and where we think the Russia-Ukraine war is headed.

item.title: India’s Strategic Predicament
item.description: On 3 September 2026, I was on CNN-News18 in India talking about how India deals with its challenging strategic environment.
item.dc:creator: John J. Mearsheimer
item.content:encoded: On 3 September 2026, I was on CNN-News18 in India talking about how India deals with its challenging strategic environment. India has powerful strategic and economic reasons to have a close relationship with the United States. But to the surprise of almost all Indians, President Trump has had a fractious relationship with their country. At the same time, India must deal with Russia and China, the latter of which represents the number one threat to India. Dealing with both of those great powers is not a straightforward matter, because how India interacts with them affects Delhi’s relations with the United States. On top of all this, India is a key member of both BRICS and the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO), two of the key institutions in the so-called Global South, which increasingly serves as a counterweight to the United States and the West more generally. In this show, I discuss the various problems India faces and how it is trying to deal with them.

item.title: The Dream Is Still Alive!
item.description: On 2 September 2026, I was on “Switzerland” with Tom Switzer, who spent most of the show putting forth the argument, which he does not believe, that is now being made by a handful of supporters of the Iran war.
item.dc:creator: John J. Mearsheimer
item.content:encoded:
On 2 September 2026, I was on “Switzerland” with Tom Switzer, who spent most of the show putting forth the argument, which he does not believe, that is now being made by a handful of supporters of the Iran war. They maintain that the ongoing economic blockade + the newly announced Bessent strategy will strangle the Iranian economy to the point where there is either regime change or abject surrender by the present regime.

Unsurprisingly, I made the argument that this approach is not going to work. There is no question the US and Israel have already inflicted enormous pain on Iran and crippled its economy, but getting Iran to surrender or producing a popular uprising is another matter. Indeed, there is hardly any evidence this approach is working, and it is clear that the widely trumpeted Bessent strategy never stood a chance of succeeding. It was dead on arrival. Moreover, there are many countries — China, Russia, and Turkey among them — who want to see Iran win the war and will help it survive. On top of that, Iran is facing an existential threat from the US and Israel, which incentivizes Iranians to fight to the death. Finally, there is no case in the historical record where one country defeated an adversary with economic pressure alone.

item.title: Still Waiting for D-Day
item.description: On 31 August 2026, I was on “Judging Freedom” talking about Iran and Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: John J. Mearsheimer
item.content:encoded:
On 31 August 2026, I was on “Judging Freedom” talking about Iran and Ukraine. I made the case that despite all the hype in the West about how well Ukraine is doing in its war with Russia, the fact is that the Russians are winning the war and there is nothing Ukraine can do to reverse the tide.

On Iran, the Judge pressed me to explain what is going on with Scott Bessent’s strategy to isolate Iran by forcing countries around the world to cut off all economic intercourse with Tehran. D-Day, the Treasury Secretary told us last week, is imminent, and any country that continues trading with and investing in Iran is going to pay a huge economic price. Of course, there is hardly any chance this strategy will work, and unsurprisingly Bessent has not told us when D-Day is coming. In the meantime, he has targeted one Egyptian bank that operates in Abu Dhabi. He doesn’t appear to be packing much of a punch.

At the same time, President Trump has just restarted the tit-for-tat air campaign that he abandoned at the end of July, because it was not working. In fact, we were recently told that using military force against Iran was no longer necessary because the US blockade of the Strait coupled with the Bessent strategy would give us huge coercive leverage over Iran. We had found the formula for success.

But it appears that there has been a change in Trump’s thinking. Might it be because he and his advisors understand that the Bessent strategy will not work?

Why should a tit-for-tat strategy work now when it failed in July?

item.title: The Mother of All Strategic Blunders
item.description: On 28 August 2026, I was on “The Chris Hedges Report” talking mainly about the ongoing disaster in Iran.
item.dc:creator: John J. Mearsheimer
item.content:encoded:
On 28 August 2026, I was on “The Chris Hedges Report” talking mainly about the ongoing disaster in Iran. Chris was interested in pushing me to explain why I believe the Iran war is the greatest strategic blunder in US history. Of course, that is really saying something when you realize it has at least two serious competitors that took place during Chris’s and my lifetimes: the Vietnam and Iraq wars.

Iran is number one in my opinion, because 1) we went into that war based on the false claim that Iran was on the verge of acquiring a nuclear weapon; 2) we had a theory of victory — air power alone would produce regime change — that has never worked and was not going to work this time; 3) we had no contingency plan for dealing with the likelihood that Iran would close the Strait of Hormuz; 4) we failed to achieve any of our four principal objectives — regime change, ending Iran’s nuclear enrichment capability, ending Iran’s long-range missile capability, and ending Iran’s support for Hamas, Hezbollah, and the Houthis; 5) the Strait was closed, which has already done significant damage to the international economy and could do much more — remember President Trump worries about following in Herbert Hoover’s footsteps; 6) we seriously undermined our carefully crafted alliance structure in the Gulf; 7) virtually all of our bases in the region have either been badly damaged or destroyed, to the point where we have moved most of our military assets out of the Gulf region and will probably not be able to return; 8) we have run down our stocks of key weapons to the point where we have weakened our deterrent postures in East Asia, Europe, and even the Western Hemisphere; 9) we have done enormous damage to our reputation as a reliable and wise ally; 10) we have markedly improved Iran’s strategic position in the Gulf region; and 11) there does not appear to be much chance — perhaps no chance — that we will get a nuclear deal of any sort with Iran, which was once considered of the utmost importance. In fact, there is a reasonable chance Iran will acquire nuclear weapons. President Trump has certainly given Iranian leaders — and other leaders of non-nuclear states around the world — a powerful incentive to acquire a nuclear deterrent.

It is difficult to imagine a more stunning strategic failure.

item.title: Why The World Is So Dangerous
item.description: On 27 August 2026, I was on Glenn Diesen’s popular podcast, where we had a wide-ranging discussion about the structural changes that have taken place in the international system since the Cold War that first led us into the unipolar moment — which many people viewed as the “end of history” — and then into the new multipolar world — which is downright dangerous and promises to remain so.
item.dc:creator: John J. Mearsheimer
item.content:encoded:
On 27 August 2026, I was on Glenn Diesen’s popular podcast, where we had a wide-ranging discussion about the structural changes that have taken place in the international system since the Cold War that first led us into the unipolar moment — which many people viewed as the “end of history” — and then into the new multipolar world — which is downright dangerous and promises to remain so.

I emphasized that those structural changes not only had an effect on how states behave, but the movement from unipolarity to multipolarity also left most academics and most members of the foreign elite ignorant of how great power politics work. After all there was only one great power in unipolarity, so great power politics was effectively taken off the table. Of course, it has come back with a vengeance. Our elites, however, both inside and outside universities, are still stuck in time, imagining that anyone who thinks in terms of basic realist logic is a dinosaur. One can rest assured that Chinese, Iranian, and Russian leaders don’t have that problem. Moreover, those same Western elites have little knowledge of nuclear strategy and deterrence theory, because those subjects were of little relevance during the unipolar moment.

item.title: The World’s Rooting for Iran
item.description: On 26 August 2026, I was on the “Deep Dive” with Lt.
item.dc:creator: John J. Mearsheimer
item.content:encoded:
On 26 August 2026, I was on the “Deep Dive” with Lt. Col. (ret.) Danny Davis talking about the usual subjects — Iran, Ukraine, and President Trump’s foreign policy.

As so often happens, Danny and I found ourselves trying to make sense of US and European policies that do not make strategic sense.

Of course, we both agreed that the US is doomed to fail in both Iran and Ukraine, in large part because — back to the previous point — we have a penchant for pursuing foolish policies.

I also emphasized that our standing around the world is now so low, that people all over the planet are rooting for the US (and Israel) to lose its war with Iran.

item.title: The West is Morally Bankrupt
item.description: On 25 August 2026, I was on “Judging Freedom” where the Judge and I mainly talked about the Trump administration’s latest plan to strangle Iran’s economy and get its leaders to surrender.
item.dc:creator: John J. Mearsheimer
item.content:encoded:
On 25 August 2026, I was on “Judging Freedom” where the Judge and I mainly talked about the Trump administration’s latest plan to strangle Iran’s economy and get its leaders to surrender.

In addition to talking about why this latest formula for victory won’t work, the Judge made the point that such a policy will kill many innocent civilians — many “little people that have nothing to do with governmental policy.” He then asked: “does the United States have any moral compass?”

My response was simple: “The US and the West more generally are morally bankrupt.” After all the US and its Western allies are complicit in the Israeli genocide in Gaza. Moreover they back Israel’s pogroms in the West Bank and Israel’s ongoing efforts to turn southern Lebanon into another Gaza.

For those who are convinced that the Israelis are the good guys and the Iranians are the bad guys, I have two questions: 1) when was the last time that Iran committed a genocide? 2) When was the last time that Iran initiated a war against another country?

item.title: Is Strangling Iran Going to Succeed?
item.description: On 23 August 2026, I was on “Switzerland” with Rose Kelanic and the host, Tom Switzer, talking about the likelihood that President Trump’s policy of delivering an “Economic D-Day” against Iran is likely to work.
item.dc:creator: John J. Mearsheimer
item.content:encoded:
On 23 August 2026, I was on “Switzerland” with Rose Kelanic and the host, Tom Switzer, talking about the likelihood that President Trump’s policy of delivering an “Economic D-Day” against Iran is likely to work. This policy has two dimensions: 1) a blockade of Iran, which has been in place since 14 July 2026, and 2) cutting off virtually all economic intercourse between Iran and other countries — isolating its economy — which is a new dimension that has surely been added because the blockade alone was not working well.

Both Rose, who is an expert on oil and coercion (see her book Black Gold and Blackmail: Oil and Great Power Politics) and I argued that the US is not going to succeed in its efforts to break Iran and get it to submit to Washington’s demands.

First, Iran faces an existential threat from the US and Israel, which incentivizes it to absorb huge amounts of pain before compromising, much less accepting defeat. Of course, Iran has already demonstrated that it can tolerate extreme pain of the sort the US and its allies dish out to countries on their hit list.

Second, the US threat to completely isolate the Iranian economy by punishing any country that continues to engage in economic intercourse with Tehran is not going to work. China, which is Iran’s largest trading partner, has already let it be known that it will not play along with the US. Nor will Russia or Pakistan break off economic relations with Tehran. The UAE has said that it will its cut economic ties with Iran, but Iran has made it clear that if it does so, Iran will use military force to make the UAE pay an awful price.

Third, as Iran’s threatened response to the UAE makes clear, in the unlikely event Trump’s policy begins to succeed and Iran begins to unravel, Tehran can respond by launching full-scale attacks on countries all across the region, which would not only threaten the survival of some of those countries, but would surely do egregious damage to the world economy.

Fourth, economic strangulation of the sort the Trump administration is pursuing takes time to work. But the US does not have time on its side. Not only is the world economy in a precarious state, but the midterm elections in the US are less than three months away. These two considerations, which are not unrelated, provide a powerful incentive to end the Iran war as soon as possible. In short, the US does not have the luxury of playing the long game, which is what its policy of economic strangulation demands.

There is no question that it is hard to imagine Trump surrendering to Iran’s demands. But what choice does he have at this point? The administration has made it clear that it has no military option, which is why it has turned to economic strangulation.

item.title: The US Economy and the Iran War
item.description: On 18 August 2026, I was on Rachel Blevins’ popular podcast, where we talked almost exclusively about the Iran war.
item.dc:creator: John J. Mearsheimer
item.content:encoded: On 18 August 2026, I was on Rachel Blevins’ popular podcast, where we talked almost exclusively about the Iran war. Of course, we discussed the military dimension of the war, but there is little fighting these days between Iran and the US, so there is not much new to say about that aspect of the conflict — at least for the time being! Instead, the focus is more on the economic dimension of that struggle. The US is betting it can strangle Iran’s economy to the point where Iran will concede defeat before the US is forced to do so. At the same time, the US is working overtime to deal with inflation and rising bond yields, which are caused in good part by the Iran war, and which have the potential to badly damage the US economy. Iran is effectively betting that continuing to limit the flow of oil and gas out of the Strait of Hormuz will threaten the US economy to the point where Washington, not Tehran, will cave first. Rachel and I talked just after reports began appearing in the mainstream media about a significant rise in bond yields. This subject has garnered a huge amount of attention since we talked and surely will continue to do so moving forward.

item.title: Living in Dark Times
item.description: On 18 August 2026, I was on “Judging Freedom” talking with the Judge about the Iran war, Israel’s never-ending outrageous behavior, the Ukraine war, and President Trump’s increasingly erratic behavior, all thoroughly depressing subjects.
item.dc:creator: John J. Mearsheimer
item.content:encoded: On 18 August 2026, I was on “Judging Freedom” talking with the Judge about the Iran war, Israel’s never-ending outrageous behavior, the Ukraine war, and President Trump’s increasingly erratic behavior, all thoroughly depressing subjects. Given that 1) Trump is destined to suffer a devastating defeat in Iran, 2) Ukraine & the West are almost certain to lose the Ukraine war, and 3) he has no hope of getting the Israelis to accept his peace plan for Gaza, it seems likely that Trump’s behavior will become even more erratic in the months ahead. He certainly has little cause for optimism and much cause for pessimism. On a more positive note, the Judge and I talked about Israel’s Lobby, the terrific new book by Eli Clifton and Ian Lustick. In fact, the Judge interviewed them right after he finished his interview with me. I would encourage all my subscribers to watch the interview and read the book.
